newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy Jan CPI seen steady at 2.6 pct y/y.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy Jan CPI seen steady at 2.6 pct y/y.

text.p: Italy's preliminary January annual consumer price index (CPI) is seen steady on December with a slight increase forecast on a monthly basis, a Reuter poll of 12 analysts showed on Thursday.
Analysts on average saw inflation rising by 0.2 percent month-on-month and 2.6 percent annually after 0.1 percent and 2.6 percent increases in December.
In January 1996, when national statistics institute Istat introduced a new basket of goods for CPI calculation, inflation was 0.1 month-on-month and 5.5 year-on year.

The analysts polled said although there was some uncertainty about the statistical effect due to the introduction of the new basket, annual prices this month should be in line with December's 2.6 percent.

The 11 sample Italian cities (up from 10 previously with the inclusion of the southern city of Bari from this month) will publish their preliminary CPI data on January 20 and 21. Istat will release the official national January data on February 4.

Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said on Monday that it was important to look at monthly variations in inflation and not at the year-on-year data because with the latter "you never know if the positive or negative variation is in the last month or in the month at the start (of the period)."

"The 0.1 percent for January 1996 was linked to a revision of the index. We don't know how true that data is," he said. Asked what he expected the January 1997 figure to be like, he replied. "Let's hope it's good."
The January 1997 CPI figure will be the first not to incorporate a fall of 0.04 to 0.05 percent which was a direct result of the revision of the basket in January 1996.

Noting Fazio's comments, "January will be good," said Ilaria Fornari, analyst at JP Morgan in Milan. "On a seasonally adjusted and annualised basis it would be much lower than the seasonal average of past years," she added.

Paolo Casadio, economist at Credito Italiano, said a positive effect on January data would come from cheaper car prices due to the government's new bonus scheme for motorists swapping old cars for scrap in exchange for buying a new car.
Analysts also mentioned as positive factors the fall in prices for afternoon cinema tickets, lower value-added tax on beef and unchanged rail travel prices.
On the other hand, potential inflationary effects might be seen due to the effect of recent bad weather on fresh vegatables, higher housing rents and dearer water, electricity and methane gas.
"But dearer motorway toll charges and the higher cost of some medicines will have a negligible effect," said Gianluca Sanna of Banco di Sardegna, the most optimistic of those polled.
Note: Bank of America said it had since revised its forecast to 0.2 pct m/m and 2.6 pct y/y (from 0.3 pct and 2.7 pct), but this does not affect the overall consensus forecast.
